title: The statutory inpatient exclusion in the counseling section and its federal reservation
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A closes by providing that the provisions of this section shall not apply to any drug dispensed to an inpatient at a hospital or nursing home, except to the extent required by regulations promulgated by the Federal Health Care Financing Administration pursuant to the provisions of 42 USC 1396r-8. The exclusion is keyed to the drug dispensed to such an inpatient, and what is reserved is regulations promulgated under that named federal provision.
exam_relevance: Fixes the exact terms of the statutory inpatient exclusion, which is keyed to the drug rather than to the practitioner and whose reservation names one federal provision rather than federal regulation at large.
exceptions: The exclusion yields to the extent required by regulations promulgated by the Federal Health Care Financing Administration pursuant to 42 USC 1396r-8.
common_confusions: The reservation is not a general reference to federal regulations; it names regulations promulgated under 42 USC 1396r-8.
This exclusion turns on the drug being dispensed to an inpatient at a hospital or nursing home, which is a different test from a regulation keyed to where a pharmacist is practising.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
